parser.name: agent-manual
parser.recipe: One born-digital page with a text layer; the text was read with PyMuPDF from drawing-checker's venv and every number checked against a 2.5x render of the page, with the starred footnotes' column positions read off the render (a text sweep loses which footnote sits under which column).

document_meta.title: NAS77 Unlined Flanged Bushings, RBC Aerospace Bearings journal bearings catalogue
document_meta.duplicate: 'RBC - Plain bearings (NAS77 p92).pdf' is the same page from the 2008/2011/2016 edition: its pdf page 94, printed page 92. Compared line by line against this file's text layer and by eye on a render: every number, tolerance and footnote is identical; the only differences are the printed page number (92 vs 98) and the copyright line. The two do not disagree. This event cites JB_NAS77.pdf; the other file's page would be the second source if a later edition changes.

entries.subject: NAS77
entries.note: The facts of the page that belong to the standard's size table rather than to one size.

series.text: NAS77 unlined flanged bushings. Material options: aluminum bronze, beryllium copper, alloy steel, CRES. A final size (FS) option is available.

material_codes.text: Available journal material options: A=Aluminum bronze alloy 642 per AMS 4640 (shown above); S=Steel alloy 4130 per AMS-S-6758; C=CRES type 17-4PH per AMS 5643; B=Beryllium copper per ASTM-B-196.
material_codes.note: The letter after NAS77 in the table's part-number column (NAS77A3-xxx) is the material. So A3 and C3 differ in material and nothing else on this sheet: same B, D, F and H for size 3. Which one the STEP's NAS77C3-015 instances mean is Jeff's question D4, not settled here.

bore_tolerance_B.text: Column B (bore): +.0015 / -.0000 in = +.038 / -.000 mm, printed once in the column header and applying to every size.

od_tolerance_D.text: Column D (OD): +.000 / -.0010 in = +.000 / -.025 mm in the header, UNLESS a starred footnote applies: * +.000/-.0005 in (+.000/-.013 mm), ** +.000/-.0007 in (+.000/-.018 mm), *** +.000/-.0008 in (+.000/-.020 mm). The figure prints D as '+.0000 / +.0010 UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN TABLE'.
od_tolerance_D.note: The figure's D band (+.0000/+.0010) and the table header's (+.000/-.0010) disagree in sign on the lower side. Both are recorded as printed; no consumer in this repo uses an unstarred D.

flange_thickness_tolerance_F.text: Column F (flange thickness): +.000 / -.005 in = +.00 / -.13 mm. The figure prints the same as '.062 +.000 / -.005' at the flange.

flange_od_tolerance_H.text: Column H (flange diameter): +.010 / -.010 in = +.25 / -.25 mm. The figure prints 'H ± .010'.

at.figure: H leader, left of the section

length_tolerance_L.text: L ± .005 in (figure only; the table has no L column, L is the dash number xxx).

at.figure: L leader, top of the section

chamfers.text: O.D. .005 — .015 x 45°. I.D. .025 — .035 x 45°, chamfer both ends (see note 6). Undercut .005 max.
chamfers.note: 'See note 6' points at a notes block this sheet does not carry.

absences.name: od_to_bore_concentricity
absences.why: The sheet bands the bore (B) and the outside diameter (D) each on its own and prints no concentricity, runout or wall-thickness band between them. A wall is only the difference of two catalogue numbers, which this repo does not derive.
absences.closed_by: NAS77 itself, not in data/inbox/specs/ -- unconfirmed that it states one

absences.name: flange_face_squareness_to_bore
absences.why: The flange is dimensioned for thickness (F) and diameter (H); no squareness, perpendicularity or runout of its face to the bore is printed.
absences.closed_by: NAS77 itself, not in data/inbox/specs/ -- unconfirmed that it states one

entries.subject: NAS77A3-015A
entries.note: Size 3 (.1900 in bore), dash -015 (.15 in long). The part number on the model and in Enovia. The STEP names its instances NAS77C3-015: per the family material_codes, that differs from this by the material letter only.

od_D.text: *0.3136 in / 7.965 mm, starred. The footnote in the D column reads +.000/-.0005 in (+.000/-.013 mm).
od_D.note: Inferred, not traced, because a SECOND '*' footnote, '+.000/-.0020 in (+.000/-.051 mm)', sits under the B column and no B value is starred; the star on D was taken to mean the one in D's own column. If the other one was meant the band is -.0020. Nothing in the topology cites this value.

flange_thickness_F.text: .062 in / 1.575 mm; +.000/-.005 in = +.00/-.13 mm. The sheet's own mm column is used for the band (1.575 - .13 = 1.445); the inch band gives 1.448.

length_L.text: Dash -015 = .15 in by the sheet's rule for xxx; L ± .005 in.

material_A.text: A = Aluminum bronze alloy 642 per AMS 4640.

absences.name: trailing_A_of_015A
absences.why: The sheet decodes the letter after NAS77 (material) and the dash number (length) and nothing after the dash number. The A in NAS77A3-015A is not explained; the intro lists 'aluminum coating' as a finish option but gives no code for it.

notes: Only this one page was read; the catalogue's other journal-bearing pages are not claimed.
Column H is the flange DIAMETER (the figure's H dimension runs across the flange), not a thickness; F is the thickness.
